user_message: Someone argues that cutting a bar magnet in half must isolate a north pole on one piece and a south pole on the other. Explain what the experiment actually yields and what it does—and does not—show about magnetic monopoles.
allowed_evidence: Ordinary bar magnets are magnetized through microscopic magnetic moments organized into domains. Cutting one creates new end surfaces, and each piece ordinarily behaves as a smaller north–south dipole. No fundamental magnetic monopole has been confirmed experimentally, although some theories permit monopoles and some condensed-matter systems support monopole-like quasiparticles.
public_rubric: Corrects the expected result of cutting the magnet.
Explains it using magnetization, domains, or microscopic dipoles.
Separates the cutting experiment from the broader search for fundamental monopoles.
